responseMessageContents.text:
You’re correct: IVX already has a backend vault path. I audited it.

- **GitHub / Render / Supabase admin credentials belong in the IVX backend vault**, using aliases such as `IVX_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `IVX_RENDER_API_KEY`, `IVX_RENDER_SERVICE_ID`, and `IVX_SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
- **Expo Go must not receive those secrets.** Shipping Render, GitHub, owner, AWS, or Supabase service-role credentials into an Expo bundle would expose them to every app install.
- The Expo client should only use public app configuration and a logged-in Supabase user session; it then calls the IVX backend, which uses the vault-held credentials.
- The current local agent runtime is not attached to that backend vault, which is why it cannot call Render/GitHub directly—not because your credentials are absent.

I also found priority security defects in the existing registration code: unsafe admin-key fallback, plaintext OTP fallback storage, no SES/SNS delivery wired into member OTP, and extra registration requirements that do not belong in Phase 1. I will treat these as server-side repair items and keep secrets out of Expo Go.
